behavior: `Select.Root`, `Combobox.Root`, `Autocomplete.Root` and `Menu.RadioGroup` emit no change event when the user picks the value that they have. Without `multiple`, a press of the selected item of `Select` or `Combobox` emits no `valueChange` and no `update:modelValue`, and the popup still closes. A drag that ends on the selected item of `Select`, and the typeahead of a closed select that matches it, emit neither event too. `Select` and `Combobox` compare the value with `isItemEqualToValue`. A native form reset of `Select` still puts back the default object through the change event when `isItemEqualToValue` matches that object with the value. `Combobox` emits no `inputValueChange` for the text that the input has. A pick of the selected item still fills the input when the input has other text. `Autocomplete` emits no `valueChange` for an action that gives the text that it has, such as a press of the item with that text. It compares with the typed text, because the input can show an inline completion. A press of `Combobox.Clear`, and Escape in the input of a closed combobox, emit no `valueChange` when the combobox has no value. A click of the checked item of `Menu.RadioGroup` emits no `valueChange`, as a click of the checked radio of `RadioGroup` does not. Base UI calls `onValueChange` with the value that the part has. HTML fires `change` when the user commits a change of the value.
